The audit was conducted in accordance with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) guidelines for energy audits in commercial buildings. The methodology comprised of the following phases:

3.2 Phase II: Site Inspection and Measurements

On-site measurements were carried out using calibrated instruments including:

• Clamp-on power analyzers (Fluke 435)
• Lux meters
• Thermal imagers
• Ultrasonic flow meters (for chilled water flow)

Load profiles were recorded over a period of 7 days at the Central Library and 3 days at the Regional Library, Malviya Nagar, to capture weekday and weekend variations.
4. RECOMMENDATIONS

Based on the findings presented in Section 3 and the detailed facility-wise analysis in Annexure A, the following recommendations are made. documents.content:
• Lighting retrofits recommended in the previous audit (2024) have been completed in the Regional Library, Malviya Nagar, resulting in a 12% reduction in lighting load. Similar retrofits are yet to be undertaken at the Central Library.

• A significant anomaly was observed in the chiller plant operation at the Central Library. The chiller energy consumption for the audit period was 1,45,000 kWh, which is 8% higher than the baseline established in the 2023-24 audit. This warrants immediate investigation.

• No major safety violations were recorded. However, power factor penalties were observed at the Central Library in three billing cycles, indicating a need for capacitor bank maintenance.

• A total of 14 energy conservation measures (ECMs) have been identified across all facilities, with an estimated combined annual savings potential of Rs. 6.8 lakh. These are detailed in Section 7.

---

2. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE

The Energy Management Cell (EMC) of JMFC commissioned M/s GreenGrid Energy Solutions to conduct a comprehensive energy audit of all JMFC facilities for the financial year 2024-25. The scope of the audit included:

• Collection and analysis of electricity billing data from JVVNL for all facilities.
• On-site inspection of electrical installations, including transformers, distribution panels, lighting systems, and HVAC equipment.
• Review of operational schedules and maintenance logs.
• Sub-metering data analysis where available.
• Identification of energy conservation opportunities with cost-benefit analysis.

The audit team comprised of:

• Er. Rajesh Sharma – Team Lead (Certified Energy Auditor, BEE)
• Ms. Priya Menon – Electrical Engineer
• Mr. Imran Qureshi – HVAC Specialist
• Mr. Ashok Kumar – Data Analyst

Facilities covered under this audit are listed in Table 2.1.

The Energy Audit Report 2025 reports Central Library, Jaipur chiller_energy_consumption_kwh is 145000 kWh. Record status: historical.

---

3. AUDIT METHODOLOGY

The audit was conducted in accordance with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) guidelines for energy audits in commercial buildings. The methodology comprised of the following phases:

3.1 Phase I: Data Collection

Electricity consumption data was collected from JVVNL bills for all 12 billing cycles covering the audit period. Additionally, monthly sub-meter readings were collected from the Central Library, Jaipur, where sub-meters are installed for the chiller plant, lighting circuits, and miscellaneous loads.

3.2 Phase II: Site Inspection and Measurements

On-site measurements were carried out using calibrated instruments including:

• Clamp-on power analyzers (Fluke 435)
• Lux meters
• Thermal imagers
• Ultrasonic flow meters (for chilled water flow)

Load profiles were recorded over a period of 7 days at the Central Library and 3 days at the Regional Library, Malviya Nagar, to capture weekday and weekend variations.

Based on the findings presented in Section 3 and the detailed facility-wise analysis in Annexure A, the following recommendations are made.
